To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) bacteria are a rich source of bioactive secondary metabolites, and (ii) new methods for discovery of novel bioactive secondary metabolite producers are needed to keep the pipeline for novel drugs from drying out

(i) the use of new bacterial species, new isolation methods and new genome mining approaches can yield novel bioactive compounds, and (ii) these approaches can be combined with synthetic biology to engineer biosynthetic pathways for novel bioactive natural products.

(i) the genome mining and bioprospecting approaches have been used to discover novel bioactive compounds produced by bacteria and (ii) the novel compounds have been discovered from bacteria previously unknown to produce bioactive compounds, from non traditional environmental nich and by using novel approaches to isolate bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel natural products from bacteria.
the isolation, characterization and biosynthesis of novel bioactive natural products.
the development of novel approaches for the discovery of new bioactive natural products with potential therapeutic value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacterial natural products are still a viable source of bioactive compounds, but that the approaches used for their identification need to be updated.
bioprospecting is a very powerful and efficient tool for discovering novel bioactive compounds from bacteria.
the future for novel bacterial metabolites as drug candidates is very bright.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach for the discovery of novel bacterial natural products.

we have discovered a number of novel bacterial species that produce bioactive compounds and we have identified the biosynthetic gene clusters for the production of these compounds and have engineered their expression in heterologous hosts.
bioprospecting and genome mining are complementary and should be combined to yield maximum benefit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time has come to abandon traditional bioprospecting of bacteria for novel bioactive compounds in favor of more sophisticated approaches based on modern genomic and bioinformatic tools.
the pipeline for discovery of novel natural products is far from exhausted, and that there is a lot more to be learned about bacterial secondary metabolome and its biotechnological potential.
the pipeline for new natural products from bacteria is not running dry.
